To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the topology of biological interaction networks can be used to predict the impact of biochemical perturbations with high accuracy.

the knowledge of the topology of biochemical networks allows to predict the perturbation patterns observed experimentally with 65% to accuracy, even in the absence of kinetic parameters, and that this accuracy can be further improved up to 80%, by leveraging key network properties.
the steady advances made in mapping out the topologies of biological networks allow to accurately predict the impact of perturbations on biological systems.

the question of whether we can make reasonably good predictions about the impact of perturbations on a system without knowing its dynamics, only knowing its topology.
the development of new mathematical models of biochemical systems.
understanding the dynamics and function of biological networks, and in particular with understanding the effects of genetic and pharmacological perturbations on these systems.
